questions.prompt: Erase fTPM NV for factory reset
questions.help: When a new CPU is installed, select [Enabled] to reset fTPM. If you use a system with BitLocker or encryption enabled, the system will not boot without the recovery key. Select [Disabled] to keep the existing fTPM records and continue booting; unless fTPM is reset (re-initialized), the new processor cannot enable fTPM. You can reinstall the old processor to recover TPM-related keys and data.

Sets the VRM switching frequency. VRM switching frequency affects transient response and VRM component temperatures. Setting a higher switching frequency will result in better transient response at the expense of higher VRM temperatures. Active cooling of the VRM heatsink is recommended when running high CPU voltage and high load-line calibration values. * Do not remove the VRM heatsink.

The switching frequency will affect the VRM transient response speed and the component thermal production. Configure a higher frequency to get a quicker transient response speed. Min.: 250KHz | Max.: 500KHz | Manual frequency step: 50KHz

Curve Shaper is an advanced overclocking tuning suite utilizing the same "Curve optimizer" steps. It changes variable voltage across all cores for finite (overlapping) frequency and temperature regions. This can be used to more precisely tune the voltage required by your system. In general, Low temperature corresponds to idle temps, Med Temperature corresponds to 1T/Gaming Workloads, and high temperature is for stress tests. Additionally, Min and Low frequencies are idle/background tasks, Medium is high core count workloads, and high and Max frequency are for gaming and 1T workloads These settings work as "bands" so you may find that for particular cases several settings impact the behavior. Ex, A workload running at 65 Celsius will likely be influenced by Low temp and Med temp values. Workloads lower than 65C will be more impacted by Low. Workloads above 65C will be more impacted by Medium.
Determines the direction of the shift. Positive shifts the curve up to use higher voltages. Negative shifts the curve down to use lower voltages
Determines the magnitude of the shift to be made (entered in whole numbers) the larger the value entered the larger the magnitude of the shift
